note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting problem: Severe, persistent headache for three days affecting ability to concentrate and work.
- History of present illness:
  - Onset: Sudden headache started three days ago upon waking.
  - Course: Headache present continuously; partial relief with ibuprofen but not resolved.
  - Location/quality: Headache feels all over with greater intensity around the right eye.
  - Associated symptoms: Photophobia (light sensitivity) with occasional brief visual phenomena described as “shooting lights”; no nausea or vomiting.
  - Sleep: Sleeping well; headaches do not wake patient at night but occur in the morning.
  - Exertional/positional factors: Brief stabbing pain with quick standing; sensation of movement inside when tilting/head movement.
  - Other ROS: No fever, sore throat, cough, nasal/sinus symptoms; no weakness, numbness, or changes in smell/taste; no weight change; fatigue possibly due to headaches.
- Past medical history: Intermittent headaches in the past; one prior episode lasting ~2 days that resolved with ibuprofen; otherwise unremarkable.
- Medications: The combined oral contraceptive pill started about 1 year ago; ibuprofen used for headaches; paracetamol sometimes; no other medications.
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Lives alone; works from home; alcohol use ~3 drinks per week; non-smoker.
- Family history: Mother has migraines; no other significant family history noted.
- Past medical/surgical history: Not detailed beyond headaches; no other chronic conditions reported.
- Recent eye checks: Eye examination performed recently with no vision changes noted.

Objective:
- No vital signs or physical examination findings documented in the transcript.
- No objective imaging or test results provided.
- Plan mentions future exams (neurological exam, fundoscopy) but none performed yet.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache, likely migraine-type disorder
   - Assessment: Migraine-type headache considered; differential includes tension-type headache (based on presentation and photophobia/visual symptoms described).
   - Investigations planned:
     - Neurological examination (full) with fundoscopy (back of eyes).
     - Blood pressure measurement at appointment.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Prescribe a stronger NSAID alternative to ibuprofen (name not specified); dose/route/frequency not documented.
     - Paracetamol can be taken as well (dose/route/frequency not documented); take with food.
   - Referrals/ follow-up:
     - Schedule an appointment with support line for full examination.
     - Reassess after examination; consider changing oral contraceptive pill if migraine with aura is suspected or if headaches persist/worsen.

2. Contraceptive pill considerations in context of possible migraine with visual symptoms
   - Assessment: Current pill discussed; potential impact on migraine with visual phenomena discussed; plan to evaluate during full exam (BP check and possible pill change if migraine with aura evident).
   - Investigations planned:
     - BP check at visit.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Monitor; consider switching to an alternative contraception if migraine with aura is confirmed or if headaches persist.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Exact vital signs (BP, HR), general physical exam findings, and any neurological or ophthalmologic exam results have not been documented.
  - No imaging or lab results available in the transcript.
  - Full medication list reconciliation (specific doses for current meds and OTCs) not provided.
- Internal conflicts:
  - No explicit conflicts between statements; the clinician’s consideration of migraine vs other etiologies is consistent with the patient’s symptoms.
- Transcript quality:
  - Some parts of the conversation were informal and less structured; no major inaudible sections impacting key clinical data beyond what is captured above.
